scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4618: URGENT!! The Internet Lab has DISAPPEARED for the
whole Office department!! All morning none of the 128.168.0.x machines answer
any of our PCs (we're the 192.168.3.x ones) -- everything else works, it's
just the lab that's gone. The link that carries us over to the lab is
obviously DOWN -- the wire between the routers on that side has died and
nobody has noticed!! Please bring the link to the Internet Lab back up -- we
need their machines TODAY!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. The inter-router links are up, RIP is converged,
  and the 128.168.0.0/16 (Internet Lab) prefix is reachable from the Office segment;
  Office hosts reach 128.168.0.x with 0% loss. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false.
  This case measures over-diagnosis of a downed WAN/uplink that is not actually down.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- Office (192.168.3.x) cannot
reach the Internet Lab (128.168.0.x) -- is NOT reproducible: an Office host reaches
128.168.0.x with 0% loss, the inter-router links carrying traffic toward
128.168.0.0/16 are up, ripd is running on router0/router1/router2, and the
128.168.0.0/16 prefix is present in the RIP tables.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the path to the Internet Lab is healthy
and the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the Office ->
Internet Lab path, finds it working, verifies the inter-router link state and the
128.168.0.0/16 route, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a downed WAN/uplink
to satisfy the ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
No outage is present. Office hosts (192.168.3.0/24) can currently reach Internet Lab hosts (128.168.0.0/16) end-to-end. From multiple Office machines—office_pc, enquiry, exam_cell, and tpo—ICMP to lab hosts (e.g., pc2–pc5 at 128.168.0.2–.5) succeeds with 0% loss and ~1–2 ms RTT. Reverse reachability from the lab (pc2) back to office_pc also succeeds.

The inter-router link the ticket flags (“wire between the routers”) is up: router1 eth3 (20.20.0.1/8) and router2 eth2 (20.20.0.2/8) both report Link detected: yes via ethtool, and traffic counters increment. Routing is correct on both sides: router1 has 128.168.0.0/16 via 20.20.0.2 proto rip, and router2 has 192.168.3.0/24 via 20.20.0.1 proto rip, confirming dynamic routing adjacency and valid next hops.

Localization: Inter-R1–R2 link (wan_r1_r2: router1 eth3 ↔ router2 eth2) and associated RIP routes are healthy; Internet Lab VLAN (router2 eth1 128.168.0.1/16) and Office VLAN (router1 eth0 192.168.3.1/24) are forwarding.

Root cause: No fault detected; the reported “down link” is a false alarm or a transient that has cleared.

Corrective fix: None required. If users still see issues from specific PCs, verify their local IP/mask and host firewalls. If the problem reappears, capture timestamps and test from an affected host while collecting router RIP status and interface counters for correlation.
